text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An undiagnosed disease kills up to eight students of Katheri secondary school in eastern Kenya.
- Post-mortem released on Tuesday rules out poison as the cause of death of former government minister Davidson Kuguru.
- Italian ambassador Roberto Di Leo says it is unfair for the Kenyan government to accuse the entire Italian community of Mafia deals.
- Opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa asks for government security for all presidential hopefuls.
- President Daniel arap Moi expresses dismay over export quotas imposed on Third World countries by wealthy nations.
- Supporters of presidential candidate Charity Ngilu urge her to quit the Democratic Party of Kenya and form another political party.
- Martin Laing, chairman of the British Overseas Trade Board, says Kenya has promoted herself remarkably as a modern and liberalised market to boost investor confidence.

- Opposition Social Democratic Party of Kenya rejects the appointment of an international negotiator to facilitate the selection of a single opposition presidential candidate. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
